issues.issue: What is the proper standard of review on appeal from a Federal Court judicial review under the Access to Information Act?
issues.respondent_position: Information Commissioner argues Merck's distinct appellate standard for Access Act reviews applies, not the general Agraira standard.
issues.result_quote: the standard of review in this Court must be the one used generally in appeals of judicial review proceedings.

issues.issue: Are the names and titles of Husky's employees, in the context of the requested records, personal information under s.19(1) of the Access Act?
issues.applicant_position: Names and titles in these records are personal information; the Privacy Act has no exemption for private sector employees.
issues.respondent_position: Records are business-related and reveal nothing intimate about the employees; names are not personal information, following NavCanada.
issues.result_quote: I am unable to find that the names and titles of Husky personnel, in the context of the requested records, meet the definition

issues.issue: Did the Board err in finding the information publicly available and in exercising its s.19(2) discretion to disclose it?
issues.applicant_position: The names in the context of these records were not publicly available; disclosure reveals more than what is already online.
issues.respondent_position: Board reasonably found the information publicly available; Husky bore the onus and filed no evidence on the employees' internet postings.
issues.result_quote: In my opinion, Husky has not shown any reason why this exercise of discretion was unreasonable.
